subject: Recap: Conversational AI burst capacity & ingestion qualification
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma@lumahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-30T10:00:00-07:00
Subject: Recap: Conversational AI burst capacity & ingestion qualification

Hi Emma — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary of pain points you shared:
- Nightly batch influx and marketing-driven bursts create 3x traffic spikes (peak windows ~20–40 minutes) and cause request-level latency > 1.2s on current hosted endpoints.
- Cost per active session has crept up ~28% in the last quarter due to repeated re-runs and lack of prefix/KV caching.
- Ingestion pipeline (message normalization + enrichment) is brittle; engineering wants to avoid early tokenization on the app side to keep prompts stable.

Goals you mentioned:
- Support steady-state 50 req/s with capacity to absorb 200 req/s bursts during campaigns.
- Reduce per-session token cost by ~25–35% while maintaining current generation quality.
- Run a 6-week pilot to validate latency SLOs and cost delta before committing to reserved capacity.

Redwood proposal (high-level):
- Pilot: Dedicated pool sized for steady-state + configurable burst credits (can throttle to fallback model variant). 6-week scope: workload capture, KV/prefix cache enablement, quantization test on a staging copy, and integration checklist.
- Cost controls: Suggest Redwood Optimize recommendations (batching windows + cache lifetimes) and per-route token profiling.
- Deliverables: pilot scope doc, estimated TCO, benchmark runbook, and a success criteria checklist (latency < 300ms p50 during steady-state, < 800ms p95 under 2x burst, token cost reduction target).

Next steps I propose:
1) Share the high-level pilot plan (attached) and a preliminary capacity/pricing draft from our side.
2) Intro to procurement for budget alignment (please loop in the person who owns purchase approvals).
3) Schedule a 30–45 minute scoping call next week to map traffic patterns and tokenization flow.

Attachments: high_level_pilot_plan.pdf (pdf)

If that aligns, I’ll pull in our pricing lead to draft a dedicated proposal and a provisional timeline (pilot in October, decision by mid-November).

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

Thanks Priya — this is helpful and accurate. A few clarifications and context from our side: 

- Spot on on the bursts. Campaign-triggered traffic is our biggest operational headache; we currently spike for ~25–35 minutes and then settle.
- Cost reduction target is important — our CFO has pushed for any work that reduces monthly inference spend by at least 20%.
- On ingestion: engineering prefers we pass raw messages to Redwood and let the model-side prompts handle normalization; they’re worried about app-side tokenization version drift.

Procurement/contact: please include Kevin Ortiz (kevin@lumahealth.com) on any budget/procurement threads — he owns vendor contracts.

Timeline: decision window is roughly Nov 15; we’d like a pilot start in early October (2–3 weeks of setup + 4 week run). Budget is constrained, so including a committed reserved option with a clear upsell path would help our internal approvers.

Can we do a scoping call on Thursday 10/1 between 10–11am PT? I can make that work.

Putting in a quick internal note after seeing Priya’s recap and Emma’s reply. Strategic suggestions for an upsell-ready pilot: 

- Offer a two-stage commercial path: 6-week paid pilot (small committed spend) -> month-to-month Dedicated with burst credits -> annual reserved commit if SLA and cost targets met. This frames the pilot as evaluation with an easy conversion.
- Include Redwood Optimize as an add-on for the pilot (analytics + batching suggestions) — it usually surfaces 15–30% token efficiency gains quickly.
- Proposed pricing model: pilot fixed fee + consumption; provide optional reserved pricing tiers and a fast-commit discount if they sign by Nov 15. I started a draft pricing workbook (attached).
